react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolites converge overwhelmingly on the arachidonic acid cascade, a major inflammatory lipid signalling network. Across three independent enrichment paradigms — multi-database ORA (RaMP-DB FDR 9.2×10⁻¹⁸), m/z network activity (Mummichog p=6.7×10⁻⁴), and KEGG-specific PSEA (MetaboAnalystR p=7.5×10⁻⁸) — the same biological module emerges as the dominant signal. The six metabolites resolved are all structurally confirmed derivatives of arachidonic acid (C20:4 ω-6): the 5- and 15-lipoxygenase products 5(S)-HETE and 15(S)-HETE, the trihydroxy triene 11,12,15-THETA, the unstable epoxide leukotriene A4, and the cyclopentenone prostaglandin 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ2. These compounds represent three canonical enzymatic branches of the cascade: the 5-LOX route toward leukotrienes, the 12/15-LOX route toward HETEs and triols, and the COX/PGDS route toward J-series prostaglandins. The enrichment fold (857× in SMPDB) and the near-complete overlap in mummichog (13 of 13 mapped metabolites) indicate that treatment strongly perturbs the entire hub upstream of these branches. The seventh input, CDP, was a singleton hit in unrelated pyrimidine/glycerophospholipid modules and is excluded from the consensus. The arachidonic acid pool itself is elevated, consistent with phospholipase A2 activation driving the observed downstream eicosanoid storm. These findings point to a global activation of lipid mediator biosynthesis with coordinated elevation of pro-inflammatory (leukotriene A4, 5-HETE) and anti-inflammatory/PPARγ-active (15-deoxy-PGJ2) arms — a pattern characteristic of acute inflammatory challenge or pharmacological COX/LOX inhibition rebound.
